Hello @boston_young, since the tracking sprints are your core offer, one thing worth checking on every store before touching anything else: whether Shopify’s own Meta sales channel is firing purchase events at the same time as your custom Conversions API pipeline. After Additional Scripts was retired a lot of stores still have that native channel connected, and it sends its own server events with its own event_id. When that happens your event_id dedup quietly fails, because the browser Pixel and your server pipeline match on one id while the native channel sends a second, different one, so Meta counts the purchase twice. The fix is usually to pick one source of truth for the server side and switch the other off, then confirm in Events Manager that each purchase shows one server event and one browser event deduplicated against it.

For the GA4 side, the Customer Events pixel runs in a sandbox with no access to window or the data layer, so a client only approach drops conversions on payment providers that redirect away from the thank you page. Sending the purchase server side through the Measurement Protocol with the same transaction id is what keeps those numbers stable.

If you want the $105 test to be clean, I would scope it as a single deduplicated purchase proven in Events Manager on one store, with the acceptance criteria written down, so there is no ambiguity about whether it passed.

Hello @boston_young, since the tracking sprints are your core offer, one thing worth checking on every store before touching anything else: whether Shopify’s own Meta sales channel is firing purchase events at the same time as your custom Conversions API pipeline. After Additional Scripts was retired a lot of stores still have that native channel connected, and it sends its own server events with its own event_id. When that happens your event_id dedup quietly fails, because the browser Pixel and your server pipeline match on one id while the native channel sends a second, different one, so Meta counts the purchase twice. The fix is usually to pick one source of truth for the server side and switch the other off, then confirm in Events Manager that each purchase shows one server event and one browser event deduplicated against it.

For the GA4 side, the Customer Events pixel runs in a sandbox with no access to window or the data layer, so a client only approach drops conversions on payment providers that redirect away from the thank you page. Sending the purchase server side through the Measurement Protocol with the same transaction id is what keeps those numbers stable.

Hello  @boston_young , since the tracking sprints are your core offer, one thing worth checking on every store before touching anything else: whether Shopify’s own Meta sales channel is firing purchase events at the same time as your custom Conversions API pipeline. After Additional Scripts was retired a lot of stores still have that native channel connected, and it sends its own server events with its own event_id. When that happens your event_id dedup quietly fails, because the browser Pixel and your server pipeline match on one id while the native channel sends a second, different one, so Meta counts the purchase twice. The fix is usually to pick one source of truth for the server side and switch the other off, then confirm in Events Manager that each purchase shows one server event and one browser event deduplicated against it. 
 For the GA4 side, the Customer Events pixel runs in a sandbox with no access to window or the data layer, so a client only approach drops conversions on payment providers that redirect away from the thank you page. Sending the purchase server side through the Measurement Protocol with the same transaction id is what keeps those numbers stable. 
 If you want the $105 test to be clean, I would scope it as a single deduplicated purchase proven in Events Manager on one store, with the acceptance criteria written down, so there is no ambiguity about whether it passed.
